tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and state purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, and understanding their universal nonequilibrium stationary states is crucial for advancing quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The paper reviews and classifies universal behaviors using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: It provides a comprehensive classification of universality classes in driven open quantum matter, highlighting the role of dissipation and driving in determining critical phenomena.
conclusion: The review establishes a framework for understanding universal properties in driven open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Frequency Shifts Heralding Ground-state Squeezing And Entanglement Of Two Coupled Harmonic Oscillators
authors: Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, and Karol Gietka

It is often argued that two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, even when cooled to their ground state, display no inherently quantum features beyond quantized energy levels. Here, we challenge this view by showing that their classical observables encode genuinely quantum features. In par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022426] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that two coupled quantum harmonic oscillators in their ground state exhibit genuine quantum features in classical observables, specifically frequency shifts that herald squeezing and entanglement.
motivation: It challenges the common belief that coupled harmonic oscillators in the ground state have no quantum features beyond energy quantization, aiming to identify observable quantum signatures.
method: The authors analyze the classical observables of two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, deriving frequency shifts that indicate the presence of squeezing and entanglement.
result: They find that frequency shifts in the oscillators' motion can serve as heralds of ground-state squeezing and entanglement, providing a measurable signature of quantum correlations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quantum features can be encoded in classical observables of coupled harmonic oscillators, offering a new way to detect and quantify entanglement in such systems.

title: Exact Entanglement Dynamics Beyond Nearest-neighbor Dual-unitary Floquet Systems
authors: Tanay Pathak
abstract:
Author(s): Tanay Pathak

Exact results using dual unitarity largely rely on nearest-neighbor structures, while finite-range interactions typically lead to complications. Going beyond the usual nearest-neighbor setting, we introduce an analytically tractable family of finite-range kicked Ising models that admit exact closed-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080306] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an exactly solvable family of finite-range kicked Ising models that go beyond nearest-neighbor dual-unitary circuits, enabling exact entanglement dynamics calculations.
motivation: Exact results in dual-unitary circuits are typically limited to nearest-neighbor interactions, while finite-range interactions are more realistic but harder to analyze. The authors aim to extend exact solvability to finite-range settings.
method: They construct a family of kicked Ising models with finite-range interactions that satisfy a generalized dual-unitarity condition, allowing exact computation of entanglement dynamics using transfer matrix techniques.
result: They derive exact expressions for entanglement growth and show that the dynamics exhibit features distinct from nearest-neighbor models, such as modified entanglement velocities and saturation values.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of exactly solvable models for studying entanglement dynamics beyond nearest-neighbor dual-unitary circuits, offering insights into the role of interaction range in quantum information spreading.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of realizing infinite-temperature-like properties in ground states of local Hamiltonians, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors design specific local Hamiltonians and analyze their ground states, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to demonstrate extensive entanglement and other infinite-temperature characteristics.
result: They show that these Hamiltonians have ground states with extensive entanglement, mimicking properties of infinite-temperature states despite being at zero energy.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of Hamiltonians with exotic ground states, potentially relevant for understanding thermalization and information-theoretic aspects of quantum systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent time evolution simulation, which achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus than gradient-descent methods.
motivation: Quantum optimization often suffers from barren plateaus and high query complexity in gradient-based approaches. The authors aim to develop a more efficient and robust optimization technique.
method: The method uses coherent simulation of time evolution to perform optimization without gradients, leveraging quantum dynamics to explore the parameter space.
result: The proposed approach demonstrates improved query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent-based methods, as shown in theoretical and numerical analyses.
conclusion: Gradient-free quantum optimization via dynamical simulation is a promising alternative for quantum optimization, potentially enhancing performance in near-term quantum computing.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in quantum neural networks for continual learning, showing that quantum models maintain adaptability as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer inherent advantages in preserving plasticity.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, comparing with classical counterparts and examining how parameter growth affects plasticity.
result: They find that quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, avoiding the rigidity seen in classical networks, and demonstrate this through theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks provide a promising avenue for continual learning due to their ability to maintain flexibility, which could lead to more adaptive AI systems.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, achieving high accuracy with low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to QLDPC codes, which efficiently explores the most likely error patterns while maintaining a bounded search width to meet latency constraints.
result: The decoder demonstrates high decoding accuracy while satisfying latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for extensive classical computation.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction with QLDPC codes, balancing accuracy and speed.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: The goal is to enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: The authors design 'twisted color circuits' that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and they propose a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance, as demonstrated by the proposed decoder.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures, relevant to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources needed for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity has been lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a new fundamental resource theory for non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum computing, and this work aims to map out where quantum algorithms can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory frameworks.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, showing regimes where quantum advantage may be possible and others where it is not.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theoretical foundations of quantum computing, guiding future algorithm development and complexity classifications.

title: Pre-distillation Of Magic States Via Composite Schemes
authors: Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, and Haim Suchowski

Magic state distillation (MSD) is a cornerstone of fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling non-Clifford gates via state injection into stabilizer circuits. However, the substantial overhead of current MSD protocols remains a major obstacle to scalable implementations. We propose a general framewo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022415] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for pre-distilling magic states using composite schemes to reduce the overhead of magic state distillation.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but suffers from high overhead, hindering scalability.
method: The authors introduce a composite scheme that combines multiple distillation protocols or states to improve efficiency, likely through a multi-level or concatenated approach.
result: The framework demonstrates reduced overhead compared to standard MSD protocols, as indicated by the publication in Physical Review A.
conclusion: The proposed composite pre-distillation schemes offer a promising path to more efficient magic state distillation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration In Quantum Machine Learning Kernels And Barren Plateaus In Variational Algorithms
authors: Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, And Roman V. Krems
abstract:
Author(s): Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, and Roman V. Krems

We show that a parametrized quantum neural network can be used to build a nonparametric quantum kernel for machine learning that inherits the concentration properties of the neural network cost function. This construction establishes a rigorous connection between barren plateaus (BPs) in variational…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022417] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, linking two important phenomena in quantum computing.
motivation: Barren plateaus hinder the trainability of variational quantum algorithms, and exponential concentration in quantum kernels similarly limits their utility. Understanding their relationship is crucial for developing practical quantum machine learning.
method: The authors construct a parametrized quantum neural network and use it to build a nonparametric quantum kernel, then prove that the concentration properties of the neural network cost function directly translate to the kernel, establishing a formal connection.
result: They rigorously show that exponential concentration in quantum kernels is equivalent to barren plateaus in variational algorithms, providing a unified framework for analyzing these obstacles.
conclusion: This equivalence implies that techniques to mitigate barren plateaus may also address kernel concentration, and vice versa, guiding future research in quantum machine learning.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with local measurements and noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise suppresses measurement-induced entanglement, leading to a transition in the entanglement properties and affecting the classical simulability of the circuits.
conclusion: The results highlight the fragility of measurement-induced entanglement to noise, with implications for quantum advantage and error correction in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical, non-quantum features of gravity.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of gravity beyond classical and conventional quantum descriptions using information-theoretic thought experiments and feasible laboratory tests.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments, focusing on their feasibility and information-theoretic implications.
result: It provides a status update on GIE-based tests, highlighting several potentially feasible experimental proposals and their theoretical underpinnings.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer concrete ways to probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue for future laboratory tests.

title: Emergent Decoherence Dynamics In Doubly Disordered Spin Networks
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, and Ashok Ajoy

Elucidating the emergence of irreversible macroscopic laws from reversible quantum many-body dynamics remains challenging, particularly in disordered media. Here, in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, we uncover an emergent decoherence law for $^{13}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070803] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals an emergent decoherence law in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, linking microscopic disorder to macroscopic irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic laws emerge from reversible quantum dynamics is a fundamental challenge, especially in disordered media. The authors aim to uncover universal decoherence behavior in a realistic spin system.
method: They experimentally study a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, likely using dynamical decoupling or similar techniques to probe the decoherence of 13C nuclear spins coupled to electron spins.
result: They observe an emergent decoherence law that is robust to the specific disorder, suggesting a universal scaling behavior. The findings connect microscopic spin dynamics to macroscopic irreversibility.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into decoherence in disordered spin systems, with implications for quantum sensing and quantum information processing in diamond-based platforms.

title: Indistinguishable Photons From A Two-Photon Cascade
authors: Timon L. Baltisberger, Francesco Salusti, Mark R. Hogg, Malwina A. Marczak, Nils Heinisch, Sascha R. Valentin, Stefan Schumacher, Arne Ludwig, Klaus D. Jöns, And Richard J. Warburton
abstract:
Author(s): Timon L. Baltisberger, Francesco Salusti, Mark R. Hogg, Malwina A. Marczak, Nils Heinisch, Sascha R. Valentin, Stefan Schumacher, Arne Ludwig, Klaus D. Jöns, and Richard J. Warburton

Decay of a four-level diamond scheme via a cascade is a potential source of entangled photon pairs. A solid-state implementation is the biexciton cascade in a semiconductor quantum dot. While high entanglement fidelities have been demonstrated, the two photons, XX and X, are temporally correlated, t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 073603] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of indistinguishable photons from a biexciton cascade in a semiconductor quantum dot, addressing temporal correlation issues for entangled photon pair sources.
motivation: The biexciton cascade in quantum dots is a promising source of entangled photon pairs, but the emitted photons are temporally correlated, which limits their indistinguishability and suitability for quantum networking applications.
method: The authors investigate the two-photon cascade in a semiconductor quantum dot, likely using resonance fluorescence or similar techniques, and analyze the indistinguishability of the emitted photons, possibly with Hong-Ou-Mandel interference measurements.
result: They achieve high indistinguishability between the two photons from the cascade, overcoming the temporal correlation challenge, and demonstrate a viable source of indistinguishable photon pairs.
conclusion: The work advances quantum dot-based photon sources for quantum networks, providing a path to high-quality entangled photon pairs with improved indistinguishability.

title: Transient-energy-backflow-enhanced Ergotropy In An Open Qubit Quantum Battery Assisted By An Auxiliary Oscillator
authors: Shun-Cai Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shun-Cai Zhao

Decoherence and dissipation in open quantum systems generally drive quantum batteries toward passive states, thereby reducing their extractable work (ergotropy). Here, we study a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator in the presence of dephasing and diss…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023106] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how transient energy backflow from an auxiliary oscillator can enhance the ergotropy of an open qubit quantum battery, counteracting decoherence-induced passive states.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from decoherence and dissipation, which reduce their extractable work (ergotropy). The authors aim to find mechanisms to mitigate this degradation.
method: They model a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator, subject to dephasing and dissipation, and analyze the dynamics of ergotropy.
result: They find that transient energy backflow from the auxiliary oscillator can temporarily increase the ergotropy of the battery, enhancing its work extraction capability.
conclusion: The auxiliary oscillator provides a practical way to improve quantum battery performance in open systems, offering insights into energy storage and thermodynamics.

title: Directional Charging Of Topological Quantum Energy-storage Devices Driven By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, And Hongrong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, and Hongrong Li

The skin effect is a phenomenon characterized by the exponential localization of wave functions at a boundary in non-Hermitian topological systems, demonstrating potential applications in the field of quantum information. Here we explore its application in optimizing the performance of quantum energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023712] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the non-Hermitian skin effect to directionally charge quantum energy storage devices, enhancing charging efficiency.
motivation: Quantum energy storage (e.g., quantum batteries) is a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and improving charging performance is of practical interest. The non-Hermitian skin effect offers a novel mechanism for directional energy transfer.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum energy storage device coupled to a non-Hermitian topological system exhibiting the skin effect, and analyze the charging dynamics and efficiency.
result: They demonstrate that the skin effect enables directional charging, leading to faster and more efficient energy storage compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: The non-Hermitian skin effect provides a promising tool for optimizing quantum energy storage, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum technology.

title: $\mathit{In}$ situ Rewiring Of Two-dimensional Ion Lattice Interactions Using Metastable State Shelving
authors: Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, And Philip Richerme
abstract:
Author(s): Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, and Philip Richerme

Trapped-ion lattice geometries, which determine the interactions between trapped-ion qubits, are typically governed by the balance of Coulomb repulsion forces with the external trapping potential. Here we demonstrate how the effective ion lattice geometry and resulting qubit-qubit interactions may b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022425] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in-situ rewiring of trapped-ion lattice interactions using metastable state shelving, enabling dynamic control of qubit-qubit couplings.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum simulators typically have fixed lattice geometries, limiting their flexibility. The authors aim to dynamically control ion interactions to enable more versatile quantum simulations.
method: They use metastable state shelving to selectively modify the effective trapping potential for certain ions, thereby altering the lattice geometry and the resulting spin-spin interactions.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the ability to rewire the ion lattice in situ, changing the interaction graph and potentially enabling new quantum simulation capabilities.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for controlling trapped-ion quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and computation.

title: Agnostic Parameter Estimation With Large Spins
authors: Huining Zhang And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Huining Zhang and X. X. Yi

The quantum Fisher information of a quantum state with respect to a certain parameter quantifies the sensitivity of the quantum state to changes in that parameter. Maximizing the quantum Fisher information is essential for achieving the optimal estimation precision of quantum sensors. A typical quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022612] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies agnostic parameter estimation with large spins, focusing on maximizing quantum Fisher information without prior knowledge of the probe state.
motivation: Quantum sensors require optimal estimation precision, which depends on maximizing quantum Fisher information. However, in practice, the exact probe state may be unknown, so agnostic estimation is needed.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for large spin systems in an agnostic setting, likely deriving bounds or optimal strategies for parameter estimation when the initial state is not fully characterized.
result: The paper provides insights into how to achieve optimal estimation precision even when the probe state is unknown, possibly showing that certain strategies can saturate the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
conclusion: The work advances quantum metrology by addressing realistic scenarios where the probe state is not perfectly known, offering practical guidance for quantum sensors.

title: Robust Two-qubit Gates For Semiconductor Spin Qubits Based On Dynamical Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

High-fidelity two-qubit gates leverage qubit-qubit interactions and are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, environmental noise and imperfect control of the interactions are inevitable, which degrade the quality of gate operations. Here we introduce local microwave driving in conven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022613] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust two-qubit gate scheme for semiconductor spin qubits using local microwave driving and dynamical dimensionality reduction to suppress noise and improve gate fidelity.
motivation: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but environmental noise and imperfect control degrade gate quality. The authors aim to design a gate that is robust against these imperfections.
method: They introduce local microwave driving in a conventional two-qubit gate setup and apply dynamical dimensionality reduction to simplify the system dynamics, effectively decoupling from noise sources.
result: The scheme achieves high-fidelity two-qubit gates with improved robustness against noise and control errors, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a practical and robust method for implementing two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, advancing the feasibility of scalable quantum computing.

title: Quantum Coherence And Entanglement In Wireless Quantum Batteries
authors: Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, and Dong Wang

We investigate the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment. By employing a unified resource-theoretic analysis, we elucidate the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022420] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of wireless quantum batteries mediated by a common structured bosonic environment, using resource-theoretic analysis to reveal the roles of non-Markovian memory and coupling symmetry.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a promising application of quantum thermodynamics, and understanding how environmental memory and symmetry affect their performance is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors employ a unified resource-theoretic analysis to study the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system, focusing on non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry.
result: The study elucidates the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in the charging process, likely showing how these factors influence energy storage and efficiency.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing quantum battery performance by leveraging environmental memory and symmetry, contributing to the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Giant-atom Quantum Battery
authors: Lei Qiao And P. Z. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Qiao and P. Z. Zhao

Most studies of quantum batteries have been restricted to conventional atoms whose size is much smaller than the electromagnetic modes. Here we propose a scheme for a quantum battery based on giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide. Specifically, both the charger and the battery are giant atoms…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022205] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum battery scheme using giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide, exploring its charging and energy storage properties.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and most studies use conventional atoms. This work aims to exploit giant atoms' unique coupling to enhance battery performance.
method: The authors model a quantum battery where both charger and battery are giant atoms coupled to a common waveguide, and analyze the dynamics of energy transfer and storage.
result: They find that giant-atom quantum batteries can achieve efficient charging and exhibit interesting non-Markovian effects due to the giant atom's multiple coupling points.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom quantum battery offers a promising platform for quantum energy storage, with potential advantages over conventional designs.

title: Mpemba Effect In Many-body Systems Near Equilibrium
authors: P. Ben-Abdallah
abstract:
Author(s): P. Ben-Abdallah

The Mpemba effect, in which a system initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one, has been observed in a wide variety of linear and nonlinear systems. Here we develop a unified framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium based on the spectral geometr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074306] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified spectral geometry framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium, showing that the effect is governed by the spectral properties of the relaxation operator.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a system initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster, has been observed in various systems but lacks a unified theoretical understanding, especially for many-body systems near equilibrium.
method: The author uses spectral geometry to analyze the relaxation dynamics of many-body systems, deriving conditions for the Mpemba effect based on the eigenvalues and eigenmodes of the relaxation operator.
result: The framework provides a general criterion for the Mpemba effect and demonstrates its applicability to several physical systems, including quantum and classical many-body systems.
conclusion: The work offers a unified explanation of the Mpemba effect in near-equilibrium many-body systems, with potential implications for controlling relaxation processes in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Dynamics With Stationary Thermal States
authors: Adrián A. Budini
abstract:
Author(s): Adrián A. Budini

Quantum and classical systems can consistently be coupled via nonunitary time-irreversible mechanisms. In this paper, we characterize which kind of corresponding dynamics converge in the stationary regime to a thermal hybrid state, that is, a density matrix that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024125] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that converge to thermal stationary states, linking nonunitary couplings to entropy maximization.
motivation: To understand how quantum and classical systems can be consistently coupled and to identify conditions under which such dynamics reach thermal equilibrium, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The author analyzes nonunitary time-irreversible coupling mechanisms and derives conditions for the stationary state to be a thermal hybrid state that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entropy.
result: The paper provides a characterization of dynamics that lead to thermal stationary states, potentially offering a framework for modeling open quantum systems with classical degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theoretical understanding of hybrid quantum-classical systems and their thermodynamic behavior, with implications for quantum thermal machines and information thermodynamics.

title: Intermodal Entanglement In A Quantum Optical Model Of High-harmonic Generation Due To The Backaction On The Driving Field
authors: Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, And Tamás Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, and Tamás Kiss

Preparation of nonclassical light with special quantum properties is essential for quantum technologies. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a process that not only enables the creation of attosecond pulses but also has the potential to generate light with intricate quantum properties. In a recent exp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033154] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates intermodal entanglement in high-harmonic generation, showing that backaction on the driving field can produce nonclassical correlations between harmonic modes.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is a promising source of nonclassical light for quantum technologies, and understanding its quantum properties is essential for applications.
method: The authors analyze a quantum optical model of HHG, focusing on the backaction of the generated harmonics on the driving field, and compute entanglement measures between the modes.
result: They demonstrate that intermodal entanglement can arise due to the backaction, with the degree of entanglement depending on parameters such as the driving field intensity and the number of harmonics.
conclusion: The findings suggest that HHG can serve as a source of entangled light, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Propagation Of The Space-time Entanglement Of Twin Photons And Twin Beams
authors: Alessandra Gatti And Enrico Brambilla
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Gatti and Enrico Brambilla

We investigate how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by multimode parametric down-conversion (PDC) propagates away from the source. We show that the entangled two-photon probability, tightly confined in space and time at the source, quickly broadens and decays out of a focal plan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033165] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the propagation of spatial and temporal entanglement of photon pairs generated by parametric down-conversion, showing that the entanglement spreads and decays away from the source.
motivation: Understanding how space-time entanglement of twin photons evolves as they propagate is crucial for applications in quantum imaging and communication.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the two-photon probability distribution for multimode parametric down-conversion, deriving expressions for its spatial and temporal correlations as a function of propagation distance.
result: They find that the entangled two-photon probability, initially tightly confined, broadens and decays out of the focal plane, indicating a decrease in entanglement strength with distance.
conclusion: The propagation of space-time entanglement is non-trivial and must be considered in practical quantum protocols relying on photon pairs.

title: Controlling Emergent Dynamical Behavior Via Phase-engineered Strong Symmetries
authors: Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, And Parvinder Solanki
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, and Parvinder Solanki

Symmetry constraints provide a powerful means to control the dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the set of accessible control parameters is often limited. Here, we show that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces a phase-dependent strong symmet…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033166] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces phase-dependent strong symmetries, enabling control of emergent dynamical behavior.
motivation: Symmetry constraints are powerful for controlling open quantum systems, but accessible control parameters are often limited. The authors aim to expand control by exploiting a tunable phase in collective coupling.
method: They analyze a cavity QED system with a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling, showing that this phase gives rise to phase-dependent strong symmetries. They likely use theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase-engineered strong symmetries allow control over emergent dynamical behavior, such as steady-state selection or suppression of certain decay channels.
conclusion: The work provides a new control knob for open quantum systems via phase engineering, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Classical Optimization Of Reduced Density Matrix Estimations With Classical Shadows Using $N$-representability Conditions Under Shot Noise Considerations
authors: Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, And Michael Streif
abstract:
Author(s): Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, and Michael Streif

Classical shadow tomography has become a powerful tool in learning about quantum states prepared on a quantum computer. Recent works have used classical shadows to variationally enforce [MATH]-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix. In this paper, we build upon previous …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033167] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes classical shadow tomography for estimating reduced density matrices by enforcing N-representability conditions, improving accuracy under shot noise.
motivation: Classical shadow tomography is a powerful tool for learning quantum states, but enforcing N-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix can be computationally expensive. The authors aim to optimize this process to make it more practical.
method: They propose a classical optimization approach that incorporates N-representability conditions into the shadow estimation procedure, considering the effects of shot noise. The method likely involves iterative refinement or convex optimization to find the best estimate consistent with physical constraints.
result: The optimized method improves the accuracy of reduced density matrix estimations compared to standard shadow tomography, especially in the presence of shot noise, while maintaining computational efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides a practical enhancement to classical shadow tomography for quantum state characterization, relevant to quantum information processing and quantum chemistry simulations.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even/odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetric qutrits, which are parameter-independent stationary states.
motivation: To achieve robust quantum information encoding using higher-dimensional systems (qutrits) with a specific symmetry, potentially offering advantages in error resilience.
method: The authors construct logical qubit states as superpositions of coherent states of U(3) for an ensemble of qutrits in a V configuration, and analyze their properties as stationary states.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states, suggesting inherent stability against certain perturbations.
conclusion: The encoding scheme provides a novel approach to robust logical qubit encoding using qutrit ensembles, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:
Author(s): Sumeja Bureković, Filippo De Luca, Michael E. Cates, and Cesare Nardini

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena that cannot be captured by equilibrium free energy approaches, necessitating a new theoretical framework.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties to describe nonequilibrium phase separation.
result: The theory yields quantitative predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes, which differ from equilibrium behavior.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonequilibrium phase separation and provides a foundation for studying active matter thermodynamics.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective measurements at the single-photon level.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks, but existing methods lack efficiency and projective measurement capability.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a setup where two microwave cavities are coupled via a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction, implementing stroboscopic measurements that repeatedly probe the itinerant photon state.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme achieves near-projective detection of single microwave photons with high fidelity, and analyze the effects of measurement backaction and imperfections.
conclusion: The proposed stroboscopic detection scheme offers a practical route for single-photon detection in microwave quantum circuits, with potential applications in quantum communication and metrology.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout for nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with molecular spins, which offer long coherence times and chemical tunability, by integrating them with mechanical detection to overcome limitations of conventional readout.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator, using mechanical detection to read out the spin state, and employ techniques to extend spin coherence and enhance sensitivity.
result: They achieve detection of nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, demonstrating the viability of the approach for quantum sensing applications.
conclusion: The work establishes a new platform for quantum sensing using molecular spins with mechanical readout, offering potential for high-resolution NMR and magnetometry.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding spectral statistics is crucial for characterizing quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, extending beyond leading order to second order in time, and consider all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal features and symmetry-class dependence.
conclusion: The results provide deeper insight into quantum chaos and may have implications for understanding thermalization and information scrambling in many-body systems.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, engineering dissipation to achieve a synchronized state with a fixed relative phase.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon with potential applications in quantum information processing and metrology, but its observation in a controlled quantum system is challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to implement two quantum van der Pol oscillators, engineering dissipation to induce synchronization, and measure the joint phase to verify the synchronized state.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization in a trapped-ion platform, which may inform future quantum technologies.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, covering theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum systems is crucial for understanding quantum information processing and verifying quantum devices. The authors aim to provide a unified computational framework based on Pauli propagation.
method: The paper develops a theoretical framework for Pauli propagation, which tracks the evolution of Pauli operators through quantum circuits, and implements it in software, demonstrating its utility on various applications.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of certain quantum circuits, particularly those with limited entanglement or specific structures, and provides a practical tool for quantum information research.
conclusion: Pauli propagation is a valuable computational method for simulating quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance. Adaptive estimation of these rates is needed to maintain high fidelity.
method: The authors propose a sliding-window approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate this into the decoder to adapt to noise fluctuations.
result: The method successfully tracks drifting error rates and improves decoder performance compared to static estimation, as demonstrated in simulations.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is feasible and beneficial for practical quantum error correction, offering a path to more robust quantum computing.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification technique that is invariant to losses.
method: The method employs phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) with simple intensity detection. By analyzing the amplified signal, they derive criteria that certify quantum non-Gaussianity without being affected by losses.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the method on a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing that it can certify non-classicality and non-Gaussianity even in the presence of losses.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and loss-invariant way to certify quantum non-Gaussian states, which is valuable for quantum information applications such as quantum communication and computation.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control electrons on a neon surface, and analyze its feasibility for qubit operation.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The work identifies a promising direction for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that inject auxiliary terms to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal cost increase, reducing circuit depth for target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are simple but often require high circuit depth for accurate simulation. Improving their efficiency is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a method to design and inject carefully chosen auxiliary terms into product formulas, correcting errors and enhancing accuracy without substantial overhead.
result: They demonstrate that the corrected product formulas achieve a given target accuracy with substantially lower circuit depth compared to standard product formulas, both in theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation, potentially accelerating quantum algorithms that rely on product formulas.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithm with systematic corrections to belief propagation, providing rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard in general, and approximate methods like belief propagation lack rigorous error control. The authors aim to develop a more accurate and efficient algorithm with provable guarantees.
method: The method builds on belief propagation by adding cluster corrections, which systematically account for correlations beyond local neighborhoods. This yields a hierarchy of approximations with increasing accuracy, and the paper provides rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence in the correction order, meaning the error decreases exponentially with the number of correction steps, while maintaining polynomial computational cost. Numerical demonstrations likely show improved accuracy over standard belief propagation.
conclusion: The proposed cluster-corrected tensor network contraction offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximating tensor network contractions, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient light-matter interfaces to enable long-distance entanglement distribution and quantum communication. Existing nodes often suffer from low photon collection efficiency or lack mechanical stability.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip, with fiber coupling for input and output, to collect photons emitted by neutral atoms. They characterize the device's performance in terms of photon extraction efficiency and stability.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact, mechanically stable form factor, suitable for quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical and scalable approach for building quantum network nodes, potentially advancing experimental quantum networks.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for various applications, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising avenue. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezing.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions, likely involving a protocol that couples the spin to the motional state to enhance displacement sensitivity.
result: The scheme achieves optimal displacement sensing, reaching the fundamental limits set by quantum mechanics, and demonstrates the advantage of spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to optimal displacement sensing in trapped-ion systems, with implications for quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability is crucial for developing reliable single-photon emitters for quantum networks and computation.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, likely using spectroscopic techniques to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter performance.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of stable single-photon sources for quantum technologies, particularly in silicon-based platforms.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, enabling real-time adaptive measurements.
motivation: Characterizing unknown spin environments in quantum systems is challenging, especially for high-dimensional parameter spaces. Existing methods are often slow or require prior knowledge of the model.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that efficiently performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it into an adaptive measurement strategy.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurements, demonstrating scalability to high-dimensional quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a fast and scalable tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating, limiting scalability. The authors aim to overcome these limitations with a non-destructive method.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to image atoms without destroying them, and use this technique for continuous loading of arrays in finite magnetic fields, which is relevant for practical quantum computing.
result: The method achieves high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading offers a scalable approach for neutral-atom quantum computing, potentially improving performance and enabling larger arrays.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient method for classically simulating small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, leveraging initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum systems is generally hard, but for small subregions of expectation landscapes, efficient classical surrogates may be possible, potentially reducing quantum resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a classical surrogate model that uses initial data from quantum computers to efficiently predict expectation values in a local patch of the landscape, likely using techniques from quantum machine learning or classical shadow tomography.
result: They demonstrate that such classical simulation can be done efficiently for small patches, with potential implications for hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to reduce quantum overhead in simulating certain quantum landscapes, contributing to the theory of quantum information and computation.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated in the paper, with potential applications in quantum error correction codes.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) for decomposing multiqubit gates and implementing quantum algorithms, highlighting simplifications like the Toffoli gate.
motivation: To survey the potential advantages of qudits over qubits in quantum computing, particularly in reducing circuit complexity and enabling more efficient algorithms.
method: The paper provides a comprehensive review of qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques, and experimental implementations, with a focus on theoretical and practical aspects.
result: It demonstrates that qudits can simplify certain quantum gates (e.g., Toffoli) and offers a survey of current experimental progress in qudit-based quantum computing.
conclusion: Qudits offer promising avenues for quantum computation, though challenges remain in hardware and error correction; the review encourages further exploration.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their growing accuracy and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and predicting them computationally can guide materials and qubit design. The review addresses the need for reliable predictions of spin-spin relaxation times.
method: The paper surveys ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for modeling decoherence in solid-state spin qubits, discussing their theoretical foundations and computational implementations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, offering a valuable tool for optimizing spin qubit platforms, though further methodological developments are needed for complex environments.

title: Robust Symmetry Breaking In Gapless Quantum Magnets
authors: Chao Yin And Andrew Lucas
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Yin and Andrew Lucas

We prove the existence of spontaneous symmetry breaking in suitably low-energy eigenstates of certain gapless and frustrated many-body quantum systems, namely symmetric quantum perturbations to classical models that exhibit spontaneous symmetry breaking of a finite group at some positive temperature…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070405] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves spontaneous symmetry breaking in low-energy eigenstates of gapless frustrated quantum magnets, linking quantum many-body physics to thermodynamic concepts.
motivation: Understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking in quantum systems is fundamental, and this work extends classical results to gapless quantum magnets, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze symmetric quantum perturbations to classical models with finite-group symmetry breaking at positive temperature, using rigorous mathematical proofs to establish symmetry breaking in low-energy eigenstates.
result: They prove that spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs in suitably low-energy eigenstates of these gapless quantum systems, despite the absence of a gap.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into quantum symmetry breaking and its thermodynamic implications, potentially impacting quantum information processing and thermalization.

title: Local-observable-guided Generative Quantum Circuits For Degenerate Ground Spaces
authors: Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), And Zizhu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), and Zizhu Wang (王子竹)

Searching for degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems is central to understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order. Although existing numerical methods can approximate individual ground states with high accuracy, recovering the full degenerate space remains a substan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022428] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a generative quantum circuit approach guided by local observables to efficiently recover degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Existing numerical methods approximate individual ground states but fail to recover the full degenerate space, which is crucial for understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order.
method: The authors propose a variational quantum circuit that uses local observables to guide the generation of states spanning the degenerate ground space, likely leveraging generative modeling techniques.
result: The method demonstrates accurate recovery of degenerate ground spaces for benchmark systems, outperforming existing approaches in efficiency and fidelity.
