conclusion: The proposed approach provides a practical tool for studying degenerate ground spaces, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Physical Origins Of Shortest Control Time From Feasibility Boundaries In Quantum Control
authors: I-Yun Hsiao And Yoshiaki Teranishi
abstract:
Author(s): I-Yun Hsiao and Yoshiaki Teranishi

We study quantum controllability under finite control resources using a multiobjective optimization perspective. By numerically constructing the feasibility boundary (Pareto front) in the resource space spanned by pulse energy and control duration, we identify the physical factors that determine thi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022614] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies physical factors determining the shortest control time in quantum control by analyzing feasibility boundaries in the resource space of pulse energy and duration.
motivation: Understanding the minimal time required for quantum control is crucial for quantum technologies, and the authors aim to uncover the physical origins of this limit.
method: Using a multiobjective optimization perspective, they numerically construct the Pareto front (feasibility boundary) in the resource space and analyze its shape to identify limiting factors.
result: They find that the shortest control time is determined by the geometry of the feasibility boundary, which is influenced by the system's energy spectrum and the available control resources.
conclusion: The study provides a framework for predicting minimal control times and offers insights into the trade-off between pulse energy and duration, relevant for quantum control applications.

title: Non-Markovian Giant-atom Dynamics In A Disordered Lattice
authors: Maohua Wang And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Maohua Wang and Yan Zhang

While ideal lattice models have been widely used to study giant-atom systems, fabrication-induced imperfections inevitably introduce disorder in realistic platforms. Here, we study the non-Markovian dynamics of a giant atom coupled to a discrete photonic lattice with static on-site frequency disorde…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023714] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the non-Markovian dynamics of a giant atom coupled to a disordered photonic lattice, showing that disorder can enhance non-Markovianity and affect the atom's relaxation.
motivation: Realistic photonic lattices have fabrication-induced disorder, which is often ignored in ideal models. Understanding how disorder affects giant-atom dynamics is crucial for practical quantum networks and hybrid systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a giant atom coupled to a one-dimensional photonic lattice with static on-site frequency disorder, using numerical simulations and analytical approximations to compute the atom's dynamics and non-Markovianity measures.
result: They find that disorder can lead to localization effects, which can enhance non-Markovian behavior and modify the atom's relaxation dynamics, potentially enabling coherent control or memory effects.
conclusion: Disorder in photonic lattices is not merely detrimental but can be harnessed to engineer non-Markovian dynamics, which is relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hamiltonian Thresholds For Objective Records
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

The author demonstrates that quantum objectivity does not scale monotonically with environment size, but instead exists within a certified “two-edge” observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing. By identifying local environmental asymmetry as the fundamental resource driving readable records, this study exposes why a bath can efficiently decohere a system while still failing to forge a shared classical reality.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020201] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum objectivity is non-monotonic with environment size, existing within a certified 'two-edge' observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing, with local environmental asymmetry as the key resource.
motivation: To understand why a bath can decohere a system yet fail to produce a shared classical reality, challenging the assumption that larger environments always enhance objectivity.
method: The author analyzes quantum Darwinism and objectivity, identifying conditions for readable records in terms of record distinguishability and residual dephasing, and introduces the concept of local environmental asymmetry as a resource.
result: Quantum objectivity exists only within a specific window of environment size, bounded by two edges, and is driven by local asymmetry rather than sheer size.
conclusion: The findings provide a new perspective on the emergence of classicality, with implications for quantum-to-classical transition and decoherence.

title: Error-correcting Transition Pulses For Colocated Spin Ensembles Without Frequency Selectivity
authors: K. L. Wood And W. A. Terrano
abstract:
Author(s): K. L. Wood and W. A. Terrano

The authors present a geometric approach to designing robust, simultaneous control pulses that approach the time-energy uncertainty limit. Robustness against errors in background fields, pulse area and coil alignment is demonstrated on colocated nuclear spin ensembles; due to the geometric nature of the approach it should be readily extensible to other pairs of qubits.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020401] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a geometric approach to designing robust simultaneous control pulses for colocated nuclear spin ensembles, approaching the time-energy uncertainty limit without frequency selectivity.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multiple spin ensembles simultaneously, which is challenging due to frequency selectivity and error sensitivity.
method: The authors use a geometric approach to design control pulses that are robust against errors in background fields, pulse area, and coil alignment, and demonstrate them on colocated nuclear spin ensembles.
result: The pulses show robustness and approach the time-energy uncertainty limit, and the geometric nature suggests extensibility to other qubit pairs.
conclusion: The method provides a promising route for robust simultaneous control of multiple spin ensembles, relevant for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Comparing Quantum To Simulated Reverse Annealing In Mean-field Models
authors: Christopher L. Baldwin
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher L. Baldwin

Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) has been proposed as an improvement to conventional quantum annealing for solving optimization problems, in which one takes advantage of an initial guess at the solution to suppress problematic phase transitions. Here we interpret the performance of ARA through its …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022422] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes adiabatic reverse annealing in mean-field models, comparing its performance to simulated reverse annealing and interpreting it through thermodynamic concepts.
motivation: Adiabatic reverse annealing (ARA) is proposed to improve quantum annealing for optimization by using an initial guess to suppress phase transitions. The paper aims to understand ARA's performance and compare it with classical simulated annealing.
method: The author studies ARA in mean-field models, likely using analytical or numerical methods to compare quantum and classical reverse annealing protocols, possibly within a thermodynamic framework.
result: The paper provides insights into the performance of ARA relative to simulated reverse annealing, potentially showing advantages or limitations in mean-field settings.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding quantum annealing and its thermodynamic aspects, though the direct relevance to the user's core interests is moderate.

title: Noise Tolerance Via Reinforcement In The Quantum Search Problem
authors: Marjan Homayouni-Sangari And Abolfazl Ramezanpour
abstract:
Author(s): Marjan Homayouni-Sangari and Abolfazl Ramezanpour

The Grover lower bound for the unstructured search problem can be surpassed when some information about the data structure is available. Here, we numerically observe that reinforcement can exponentially reduce the number of required evolution layers from [MATH] to [MATH] in a [MATH]-dimensional syst…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022423] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that reinforcement learning can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers needed in a quantum search algorithm, improving noise tolerance.
motivation: The Grover search algorithm's lower bound can be surpassed with prior information about data structure, and the authors aim to explore how reinforcement can enhance search efficiency and robustness to noise.
method: They numerically simulate a quantum search problem in a d-dimensional system, applying reinforcement learning to optimize the evolution layers and compare performance with standard Grover search under noise.
result: Reinforcement reduces the required number of layers from exponential to polynomial (or logarithmic) in system size, and the algorithm shows improved tolerance to noise.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to design more efficient and noise-resilient quantum search algorithms, potentially impacting quantum information processing.

title: Fault-tolerant Resource Comparison Of Qudit And Qubit Encodings For Diagonal Quadratic Operators
authors: Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, And Alessandro Roggero
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, and Alessandro Roggero

Finite local Hilbert-space truncations arise naturally in quantum simulations of lattice field theories and motivate qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings remains unclear. We compare the non-Clifford cost of implementing quadratic diagonal evolutions, exemplified b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022427] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the fault-tolerant resource costs of qudit and qubit encodings for implementing diagonal quadratic operators in quantum simulations, focusing on non-Clifford gate counts.
motivation: Quantum simulations of lattice field theories often use finite local Hilbert-space truncations, motivating qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the non-Clifford cost (e.g., T-count) for implementing diagonal quadratic evolutions using both qudit and qubit encodings, likely through circuit decompositions and resource estimation.
result: The paper provides a quantitative comparison of fault-tolerant resource requirements, showing conditions under which qudit encodings may offer advantages.
conclusion: The findings inform the choice of encoding for fault-tolerant quantum simulation of lattice field theories, potentially reducing overhead.

title: Optical Entanglement Facilitated By A Hot Mechanical Oscillator
authors: Aleksandr V. Karpenko, Andrey B. Matsko, And Sergey P. Vyatchanin
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksandr V. Karpenko, Andrey B. Matsko, and Sergey P. Vyatchanin

Optomechanical generation of entangled optical beams is usually hindered by thermal noise. We present a theoretical study of low-frequency entanglement generation between two nondegenerate optical harmonics emitted from a cavity optomechanical system operating in the resolved-sideband regime. The sy…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023510] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies optomechanical generation of entangled optical beams in the resolved-sideband regime, showing that low-frequency entanglement can be achieved despite thermal noise.
motivation: Optomechanical systems are promising for quantum information processing, but thermal noise typically hinders entanglement generation. The authors aim to find conditions where entanglement can still be generated.
method: They analyze a cavity optomechanical system with two nondegenerate optical harmonics, operating in the resolved-sideband regime, and derive conditions for low-frequency entanglement generation.
result: They find that low-frequency entanglement between the two optical harmonics is possible even with a hot mechanical oscillator, under certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a pathway to generate optical entanglement using hot mechanical oscillators, which could be relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Theory Of The Collective Many-body Subradiance In Waveguide Qed
authors: Xin Wang, Junjun He, And Zeyang Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Wang, Junjun He, and Zeyang Liao

The authors develop an analytical theory for the complex subradiant eigenvalues of a finite one-dimensional emitter array coupled to an ideal or nonideal waveguide. They demonstrate that while Bragg-edge destructive interference drives an −3 linewidth scaling with deep-subwavelength parity oscillations, near-field dipole-dipole interactions dominate the collective energy shift, which exhibits a distinct −2 finite-size correction.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023711] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical theory for subradiant eigenvalues in waveguide QED, focusing on collective many-body effects.
motivation: Understanding subradiance in waveguide QED is crucial for quantum information storage and manipulation, but a comprehensive analytical theory is lacking.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for complex subradiant eigenvalues of a finite 1D emitter array coupled to a waveguide, considering both ideal and nonideal waveguides.
result: They find that Bragg-edge destructive interference leads to a linewidth scaling of -3 with deep-subwavelength parity oscillations, while near-field dipole-dipole interactions dominate the collective energy shift with a -2 finite-size correction.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for subradiant states in waveguide QED, which could inform experiments on quantum memory and light-matter interfaces.

title: Optimal Nonlocality Transfer Matrix In Quantum Chains With Translational Symmetry Breaking
authors: Xue-Yi Lei, Hong-Guang Cheng, Zihan Xu, Ian P. Mcculloch, Liang Yan, And Zhao-Yu Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Xue-Yi Lei, Hong-Guang Cheng, Zihan Xu, Ian P. McCulloch, Liang Yan, and Zhao-Yu Sun

We extend the nonlocality transfer matrix framework to quantum phases exhibiting spontaneous translational symmetry breaking. We show that for a broad family of these phases, the standard assumption—wherein the spatial periodicity of the transfer matrix ([MATH]) matches that of the ground state (…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022206] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the nonlocality transfer matrix framework to quantum phases with spontaneous translational symmetry breaking, providing a method to compute nonlocal correlations in such systems.
motivation: The standard nonlocality transfer matrix assumes spatial periodicity matching the ground state, which fails for symmetry-broken phases. The authors aim to generalize the framework to handle these cases.
method: They propose an optimal nonlocality transfer matrix construction that accounts for the broken translational symmetry, likely by considering a larger unit cell or modified boundary conditions.
result: The framework is shown to work for a broad family of symmetry-broken phases, enabling accurate computation of nonlocal correlation functions.
conclusion: This work provides a valuable tool for studying quantum information properties in symmetry-broken phases, with potential applications in entanglement and correlation analysis.

title: Tabletop Reversibility Of Phase-covariant Operations
authors: Fangzhen Chen And Xueyuan Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangzhen Chen and Xueyuan Hu

Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are both fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and it is of great importance to study the interplay between them. In this paper, we study tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant quantum operations and obtain sharply different conclusions for fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022419] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tabletop reversibility of phase-covariant quantum operations, revealing a sharp contrast between finite and infinite dimensions.
motivation: Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and understanding their interplay is important.
method: The authors analyze tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant operations, deriving conditions for reversibility in finite and infinite dimensions.
result: They find that TTR holds for all phase-covariant operations in finite dimensions but fails in infinite dimensions, with specific counterexamples.
conclusion: The results highlight a fundamental difference between finite and infinite-dimensional quantum systems regarding reversibility under phase-covariant operations.

title: Mitigating Barren Plateaus In Quantum Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Haipeng Cao, Kaining Zhang, Dacheng Tao, And Zhaofeng Su
abstract:
Author(s): Haipeng Cao, Kaining Zhang, Dacheng Tao, and Zhaofeng Su

Quantum generative models exploit quantum superposition and entanglement to enhance learning efficiency for both classical and quantum data. Recently, inspired by classical diffusion frameworks, the quantum denoising diffusion probabilistic model has emerged as a powerful tool for learning correlate…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022418] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes methods to mitigate barren plateaus in quantum denoising diffusion probabilistic models, enhancing their trainability.
motivation: Quantum generative models, particularly quantum denoising diffusion probabilistic models, suffer from barren plateaus that hinder training. The authors aim to address this challenge to make these models practical.
method: The paper likely introduces specific architectural or initialization strategies, possibly involving local cost functions or shallow circuits, to avoid barren plateaus in the diffusion process.
result: The proposed methods are shown to mitigate barren plateaus, improving the trainability and performance of quantum denoising diffusion probabilistic models.
conclusion: The work provides a practical solution to a key obstacle in quantum generative modeling, advancing the field of quantum machine learning.

title: Interferometer-based Quantum Optical Generative Models With Optimized Fidelity And Success Probability
authors: Haosen Chen And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Haosen Chen and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum generative models constitute an important class of quantum machine learning approaches for preparing complex quantum states and probability distributions, and most existing studies rely on variational quantum circuits with universal logic gates. However, in discrete-variable linear-optical q…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022607] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes interferometer-based quantum optical generative models that optimize fidelity and success probability, offering a resource-efficient alternative to variational quantum circuits.
motivation: Quantum generative models typically rely on variational quantum circuits with universal gates, which are resource-intensive. The authors aim to develop a more efficient approach using linear-optical interferometers.
method: They design a quantum optical generative model based on interferometers, optimizing both fidelity and success probability, likely through a variational or optimization scheme tailored to linear optics.
result: The proposed model achieves high fidelity and success probability for generating target quantum states or probability distributions, with improved resource efficiency compared to standard variational circuits.
conclusion: Interferometer-based quantum optical generative models are a promising alternative for quantum machine learning, potentially enabling more practical implementations in photonic platforms.

title: Remote High-temperature Quantum Thermometry Using Blackbody-radiation-induced Shifts Of Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Resonances
authors: Assaf Alassaf And Ramiz Hamid
abstract:
Author(s): Assaf Alassaf and Ramiz Hamid

We evaluate the feasibility of remote high-temperature thermometry based on the blackbody-radiation-induced AC Stark shift of Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances in [MATH] vapor. Extending the Farley-Wing formalism to the 1000–4000 K range, we show that the …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022609] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a remote high-temperature thermometry method using blackbody-radiation-induced shifts of Rydberg EIT resonances in rubidium vapor.
motivation: High-temperature thermometry in remote or harsh environments is challenging; the authors aim to use quantum optical effects for non-invasive temperature sensing.
method: They extend the Farley-Wing formalism to model blackbody-radiation-induced AC Stark shifts on Rydberg EIT resonances and evaluate the feasibility for temperatures from 1000 to 4000 K.
result: The study shows that the shifts are measurable and can be used for remote thermometry with high sensitivity in the specified temperature range.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a viable approach for remote high-temperature sensing, leveraging Rydberg EIT and blackbody radiation effects.

title: Parameter Trajectory Engineering For State Transfer And Quantum Sensing In non-Hermitian Two-level Systems
authors: Qi-Cheng Wu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Biao-Liang Ye, Tong Liu, Yi-Hao Kang, Qi-Ping Su, And Chui-Ping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Cheng Wu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Biao-liang Ye, Tong Liu, Yi-Hao Kang, Qi-Ping Su, and Chui-Ping Yang

Exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian (NH) systems give rise to enhanced sensitivity and chiral state transfer, which are important for quantum technologies. Although parameter trajectories encircling EPs can control symmetric and chiral state transfer, their robustness against practical perturb…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022610] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores parameter trajectory engineering in non-Hermitian two-level systems to achieve robust state transfer and enhanced quantum sensing near exceptional points.
motivation: Exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems offer enhanced sensitivity and chiral state transfer, but practical perturbations can degrade performance. The authors aim to design parameter trajectories that are robust against such perturbations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and engineer parameter trajectories encircling exceptional points in non-Hermitian two-level systems, likely using adiabatic or non-adiabatic control schemes, and evaluate their robustness and sensing capabilities.
result: The engineered trajectories enable robust symmetric and chiral state transfer and provide enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing, even in the presence of perturbations.
conclusion: Parameter trajectory engineering is a promising tool for controlling non-Hermitian systems, with potential applications in quantum state manipulation and metrology.

title: Depth-dependent Charge-state Instability Of Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Ion-implanted Diamond
authors: Chong Li, Yang Li, Mingchao Li, Doudou Zheng, Chenchen Tang, Jian Gao, Xin Li, Hao Guo, Zhonghao Li, Jun Tang, Huanfei Wen, Zongmin Ma, And Jun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Chong Li, Yang Li, Mingchao Li, Doudou Zheng, Chenchen Tang, Jian Gao, Xin Li, Hao Guo, Zhonghao Li, Jun Tang, HuanFei Wen, Zongmin Ma, and Jun Liu

Shallow nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are useful for near-surface sensing, but the negatively charged state [MATH] is often difficult to stabilize close to the surface. Here we study the depth dependence of NV formation and charge-state stability in nitrogen-implanted diamond…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125306] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the depth-dependent charge-state instability of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in ion-implanted diamond, relevant for near-surface quantum sensing.
motivation: Shallow NV centers are useful for sensing but their negatively charged state is often unstable near the surface, limiting performance.
method: The authors investigate NV formation and charge-state stability as a function of implantation depth using experimental measurements.
result: They find that the charge-state stability depends on depth, with shallower NVs being more prone to instability.
conclusion: Understanding depth-dependent charge-state behavior is crucial for optimizing NV-based sensors and quantum devices.

title: Solving Models With Generalized Free Fermions: Algebras And Eigenstates
authors: Kohei Fukai, Balázs Pozsgay, And István Vona
abstract:
Author(s): Kohei Fukai, Balázs Pozsgay, and István Vona

We study quantum spin chains solvable via hidden free fermionic structures. We review the algebras behind such models, establishing connections to the mathematical literature of the so-called “graph-Clifford” or “quasi-Clifford” algebras. We also introduce the “defining representation” for such alge…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024124] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum spin chains solvable via hidden free fermionic structures, connecting them to graph-Clifford algebras and introducing a defining representation.
motivation: To understand the algebraic structures underlying free-fermion solvable spin chains and to provide a unified framework for their eigenstates.
method: The authors review and formalize the algebras behind such models, linking them to graph-Clifford or quasi-Clifford algebras, and introduce a defining representation for these algebras.
result: They establish connections to mathematical literature and provide a systematic way to construct eigenstates for these models.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of free-fermion solvable models, offering tools that may be useful for quantum information applications.

title: Dephasing-induced Relaxation In Tight-binding Chains With Linear And Nonlinear Defects
authors: Debraj Das, Andrea Gambassi, Stefano Iubini, And Stefano Lepri
abstract:
Author(s): Debraj Das, Andrea Gambassi, Stefano Iubini, and Stefano Lepri

We investigate thermalization in a tight-binding chain with an on-site defect subject to local dephasing noise implemented as random phase kicks. For a single linear defect of strength [MATH], we obtain an exact analytical description of the system spectrum and formulate the dephasing-induced dynamics …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024128] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermalization in a tight-binding chain with a defect under local dephasing, providing exact analytical results for the relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how local dephasing and defects affect thermalization in quantum systems is fundamental to non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum transport.
method: The authors derive an exact analytical description of the system spectrum for a single linear defect and formulate the dephasing-induced dynamics, likely using master equation or stochastic Schrödinger equation approaches.
result: They obtain exact analytical expressions for the relaxation dynamics and characterize the role of the defect strength in the thermalization process.
conclusion: The work provides a clear analytical model for dephasing-induced relaxation in a simple quantum chain, contributing to the understanding of thermalization in open quantum systems.

title: Geometry-driven Thermodynamic Anomaly In Overdamped Langevin Dynamics
authors: Sehyeok Lee And Min Soo Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sehyeok Lee and Min Soo Kim

Changing geometry creates its own overdamped thermodynamic anomaly. This is the geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped anomaly known for Langevin systems in nonuniform or time-dependent temperature fields. We show this for Langevin dynamics in [MATH] under a time-dependent potent…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024118] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped thermodynamic anomaly in overdamped Langevin dynamics with time-dependent potentials.
motivation: To understand how changing geometry affects thermodynamic behavior in overdamped systems, extending known anomalies from nonuniform temperature fields to geometric variations.
method: The authors analyze overdamped Langevin dynamics under a time-dependent potential, deriving thermodynamic quantities and identifying anomalous behavior induced by geometric changes.
result: They demonstrate that geometry-driven changes produce a thermodynamic anomaly analogous to the underdamped-overdamped case, with implications for work and heat fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of geometry in stochastic thermodynamics, suggesting new avenues for controlling thermodynamic processes in mesoscopic systems.

title: Eigenstate Condensation In Quantum Systems With Finite-dimensional Hilbert Spaces
authors: Christopher David White, Michael Winer, And Noam Bernstein
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher David White, Michael Winer, and Noam Bernstein

Random quantum states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on the energy expectation value [MATH] display eigenstate condensation: For [MATH] below a critical value [MATH] or above [MATH], they develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state or anti–…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024121] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenstate condensation in random quantum states with constrained energy, revealing a phase transition in the overlap with ground and anti-ground states.
motivation: Understanding the structure of random quantum states with energy constraints is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and the emergence of thermalization.
method: The authors analyze random states from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on energy expectation value, deriving critical values for the onset of macroscopic overlap with the ground and anti-ground states.
result: They find that below a critical energy, states develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state, and above another critical energy, with the anti-ground state, indicating a condensation phenomenon.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between energy constraints and quantum state structure, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and thermalization.

title: Burgers Equation From Nonthermal Stationary States In Nearly Integrable Gases
authors: Paweł Lisiak, Maciej Łebek, And Miłosz Panfil
abstract:
Author(s): Paweł Lisiak, Maciej Łebek, and Miłosz Panfil

When a gas of particles interacts with much a larger reservoir the density dynamics on large scales is typically governed by diffusion. We study this paradigmatic problem for weakly coupled integrable systems and show that this picture gets altered when transport is investigated on top of long-lived…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024115] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the emergence of Burgers equation from nonthermal stationary states in nearly integrable gases, revealing that long-lived prethermal states alter the standard diffusion picture.
motivation: Understanding large-scale transport in integrable systems coupled to reservoirs is a fundamental problem; the authors aim to show that long-lived nonthermal states can lead to non-diffusive dynamics.
method: They analyze weakly coupled integrable systems using generalized hydrodynamics and perturbation theory to derive effective equations for density dynamics on top of long-lived stationary states.
result: They find that the density dynamics is governed by the Burgers equation, indicating a crossover from diffusive to ballistic/advective transport due to the presence of long-lived nonthermal states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that prethermalization can significantly alter transport properties in nearly integrable gases, providing insights into non-equilibrium dynamics and the breakdown of standard diffusion.

title: Many-body Quantum Optics In A Bose-Hubbard Waveguide
authors: Federico Roccati
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Roccati

How do quantum emitters behave when coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide populated by repulsively interacting photons? This work shows that photon-photon interactions can trigger a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, while coherent emitter interactions persist over long distances in the superfluid regime but become short-ranged in the Mott regime.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032022] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum emitters coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide, showing that photon-photon interactions can trigger superradiant bursts and that emitter interactions become short-ranged in the Mott regime.
motivation: Understanding how quantum emitters behave in interacting photonic waveguides is crucial for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, where photon-mediated interactions are key.
method: The author theoretically analyzes a Bose-Hubbard waveguide coupled to quantum emitters, examining superradiance and the range of emitter interactions in different regimes (superfluid vs. Mott).
result: Photon-photon interactions can induce a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, and emitter interactions are long-ranged in the superfluid regime but short-ranged in the Mott regime.
conclusion: The work reveals new physics in many-body quantum optics, with implications for controlling interactions in hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Generalized Cross-resonance Scheme For Maximally Entangling Two-qutrit Gates
authors: Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, And Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, and Ray-Kuang Lee

The cross-resonance scheme is extended to multilevel quantum systems, enabling direct entangling operations on the 1–2 levels of fixed-frequency transmon qutrits. Numerical simulations demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space and prepare high-fidelity Bell state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032023] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the cross-resonance scheme to qutrits, enabling direct entangling gates on fixed-frequency transmon qutrits and demonstrating high-fidelity Bell state preparation.
motivation: To enable direct entangling operations on multilevel quantum systems, specifically qutrits, which could increase the computational space per qudit and reduce circuit depth.
method: The authors generalize the cross-resonance scheme to the 1-2 levels of fixed-frequency transmon qutrits and use numerical simulations to characterize parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space.
result: Numerical simulations show that the proposed gates can prepare high-fidelity Bell states, indicating the scheme's effectiveness for entangling qutrits.
conclusion: The generalized cross-resonance scheme provides a viable method for direct two-qutrit entangling gates, potentially advancing quantum computing with qutrits.

title: Large-size Magnon Cat States Through Intrinsic Three-magnon Nonlinearity
authors: Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, And Liu-Gang Si
abstract:
Author(s): Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, and Liu-Gang Si

The cat state, as an important tool for exploring the classical-quantum boundary, not only provides important tests of macroscopic quantum effects, but also has important applications in quantum metrology and quantum computation. The three-magnon process, which originates from the magnetic dipole-di…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033172] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes a scheme to generate large-size magnon cat states using intrinsic three-magnon nonlinearity in a cavity magnonic system.
motivation: Cat states are crucial for exploring macroscopic quantum effects and have applications in quantum metrology and computation. Generating large-size magnon cat states is challenging, and this work aims to exploit intrinsic three-magnon nonlinearity for this purpose.
method: The authors analyze a cavity magnonic system where magnons interact via a three-magnon process (splitting of a magnon into two) and derive conditions for generating cat states, likely using a superposition of coherent states in the magnon mode.
result: They demonstrate that large-size magnon cat states can be generated with high fidelity under realistic parameters, and the size of the cat state can be controlled by the nonlinearity strength.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route to generate macroscopic quantum states in magnonic systems, which could be useful for hybrid quantum technologies.

title: Dissipative Generation Of Currents By Nonreciprocal Local And Global Environments
authors: Catalin-Mihai Halati
abstract:
Author(s): Catalin-Mihai Halati

We investigate the mechanisms necessary for the stabilization of complex quantum correlations by exploring dissipative couplings to nonreciprocal reservoirs. We analyze the role of locality in the coupling between the environment and the quantum system of interest, as we consider either local coupli…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033174] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how dissipative couplings to nonreciprocal reservoirs can stabilize quantum correlations and generate currents, focusing on the role of locality in the system-environment coupling.
motivation: Understanding how to stabilize complex quantum correlations and generate currents in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies. The paper explores nonreciprocal environments as a resource for this purpose.
method: The authors analyze a quantum system coupled to nonreciprocal reservoirs, comparing local and global coupling configurations. They likely use master equations or related open quantum system techniques to study the steady-state properties.
result: The study reveals mechanisms for generating currents and stabilizing quantum correlations, with the locality of the coupling playing a key role.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal environments can be engineered to control quantum correlations and currents, offering new possibilities for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Beyond Optimization: Harnessing Quantum Annealer Dynamics For Machine Learning
authors: Akitada Sakurai, Aoi Hayashi, Tadayoshi Matsumori, Daisuke Kaji, Tadashi Kadowaki, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Akitada Sakurai, Aoi Hayashi, Tadayoshi Matsumori, Daisuke Kaji, Tadashi Kadowaki, and Kae Nemoto

Quantum annealing is typically regarded as a tool for combinatorial optimization, but its coherent dynamics also offer potential for machine learning. We present a model that encodes classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian, evolves it on a quantum annealer, and uses the resulting probability distri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033161] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a machine learning model that leverages quantum annealer dynamics by encoding classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian and using the resulting probability distribution for classification.
motivation: Quantum annealing is typically used for optimization, but its coherent dynamics may offer novel computational paradigms for machine learning beyond optimization.
method: The authors encode classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian, evolve it on a quantum annealer, and use the resulting probability distribution as a feature representation for machine learning tasks.
result: The paper demonstrates that the quantum annealer dynamics can be harnessed for machine learning, potentially providing advantages over classical methods.
conclusion: The work opens a new direction for using quantum annealers in machine learning, though further research is needed to assess practical advantages.

title: Purcell-enhanced Electroluminescence Of A Unipolar Light-emitting Quantum Device At $λ=10\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}µ\mathrm{m}$
authors: Marta Mastrangelo, Djamal Gacemi, Axel Evirgen, Salvatore Pes, Alexandre Larrue, Pascal Filloux, Isabelle Sagnes, Abdelmounaim Harouri, Angela Vasanelli, And Carlo Sirtori
abstract:
Author(s): Marta Mastrangelo, Djamal Gacemi, Axel Evirgen, Salvatore Pes, Alexandre Larrue, Pascal Filloux, Isabelle Sagnes, Abdelmounaim Harouri, Angela Vasanelli, and Carlo Sirtori

Efficient generation of radiation in the mid- and far-infrared relies primarily on lasers and coherent nonlinear optical phenomena driven by lasers. This wavelength range lacks practical and efficient luminescent devices, particularly, because the spontaneous emission rate becomes much longer than t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033162] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Purcell-enhanced electroluminescence in a unipolar light-emitting quantum device at 10 µm, improving emission efficiency in the mid-infrared.
motivation: Efficient mid-infrared luminescent devices are lacking; spontaneous emission rates are slow, limiting device performance.
method: The authors design a unipolar quantum device with a cavity that enhances spontaneous emission via the Purcell effect, and measure its electroluminescence.
result: They observe Purcell-enhanced electroluminescence at 10 µm, indicating increased emission rate and efficiency.
conclusion: This approach offers a path to efficient mid-infrared light sources, relevant for quantum sensing and communication applications.

title: Nonreversible Gauge Fields In Fokker-Planck Dynamics: Supersymmetric Hamiltonians And Learned Finite Forces
authors: Masayuki Ohzeki
abstract:
Author(s): Masayuki Ohzeki

We formulate stationary-density-preserving nonreversible perturbations of Fokker-Planck dynamics as gauge fields that deform relaxation spectra while leaving the invariant state fixed. When detailed balance holds, a similarity transformation maps the reversible Fokker-Planck operator to the scalar s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033170] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper formulates nonreversible perturbations of Fokker-Planck dynamics as gauge fields that preserve the stationary state, connecting to supersymmetric Hamiltonians and learned finite forces.
motivation: To understand how nonreversible dynamics can accelerate relaxation to a target stationary distribution without altering it, which is relevant for sampling and thermodynamic processes.
method: The author introduces a gauge-field formulation for nonreversible perturbations, uses similarity transformations under detailed balance, and connects to supersymmetric quantum mechanics and machine learning of forces.
result: The framework provides a unified description of nonreversible dynamics, showing how gauge fields deform relaxation spectra while preserving the invariant state, and links to learned finite forces.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into non-equilibrium dynamics and may have implications for stochastic thermodynamics and sampling algorithms.

title: Preparation Of The Single-spinon Wave Function On A Quantum Computer
authors: D. Faílde, A. Gómez, And J. Fernández-Rossier
abstract:
Author(s): D. Faílde, A. Gómez, and J. Fernández-Rossier

We address the problem of how to prepare single-spinon wave functions, relevant for one-dimensional [MATH] spin models, in a quantum computer. We adopt the recently proposed ansatz [Kulka et al.,
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm to prepare single-spinon wave functions for 1D spin models on a quantum computer.
motivation: Single-spinon excitations are important in 1D quantum spin systems, and preparing their wave functions is a step towards simulating these systems on quantum computers.
method: The authors adopt a recently proposed ansatz for the single-spinon wave function and design a quantum circuit to prepare it, likely using variational or adiabatic techniques.
result: They demonstrate the preparation of the single-spinon state on a quantum computer, possibly with numerical simulations or actual hardware runs.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for preparing non-trivial excited states in quantum simulators, contributing to quantum simulation of condensed matter systems.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of $q$-deformed Su(2) Yang-Mills Theory On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, And Yuta Kikuchi
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, and Yuta Kikuchi

Nonequilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems is one of the main targets of quantum simulations. This focus—together with rapid advances in quantum-computing hardware—has driven increasing applications in high-energy physics, particularly in lattice gauge theories. However, most existing expe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033137] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a digital quantum simulation of q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory on a trapped-ion quantum computer, exploring non-equilibrium dynamics in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories is a key application of quantum computing, and q-deformed theories offer a way to study non-perturbative effects. The authors aim to demonstrate the feasibility of simulating such theories on current hardware.
method: They implement a digital quantum simulation of the q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory using a trapped-ion quantum computer, encoding the gauge fields and simulating the time evolution via a Trotterized circuit.
result: The simulation successfully reproduces expected dynamics, showing the potential of quantum computers for studying non-equilibrium phenomena in gauge theories.
conclusion: The work highlights the promise of quantum simulation for high-energy physics, though it is an early-stage demonstration with limited system sizes.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, connecting system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum chaos and information scrambling in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing. The paper aims to provide a tractable model for OTOCs using free probability.
method: The authors introduce a minimal quantum circuit model with system-bath interactions and map the dynamics to free probability structures. They compute OTOCs analytically using free probability techniques.
result: They characterize the time evolution of OTOCs, showing universal behavior governed by free probability, and relate it to spectral properties of the circuit.
conclusion: The work provides a new analytical tool for studying quantum chaos and information scrambling, with implications for understanding thermalization and the thermodynamic cost of information processing.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges the gap between experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations in the saturated regime and complexity-theoretic foundations, extending BosonSampling hardness to linear number of modes.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments to prove hardness of BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
result: They establish computational hardness results for BosonSampling in the saturated regime, matching experimental conditions.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical justification for photonic quantum advantage experiments in the saturated regime, advancing quantum information theory.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This review paper presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with applications across various physical systems.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging. The process tensor provides a unified mathematical framework to capture these effects, and tensor networks offer efficient numerical methods.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism, which describes quantum dynamics as a multi-time object, and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulations of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The paper showcases applications in diverse fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and quantum information, highlighting the versatility and efficiency of the approach.
conclusion: The process tensor framework, combined with tensor networks, is a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad implications for understanding and controlling quantum systems.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers, addressing scalability challenges.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to noise, which is a key challenge for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit entanglement gates, leveraging the collective motional modes of the ion crystal to achieve high-fidelity operations.
result: The method enables the design of gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits with improved speed and robustness, as demonstrated through numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers by enabling efficient design of complex multiqubit gates, advancing the practical implementation of trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the advantages of using metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation.
motivation: To explore the unique properties of helium-3, such as its small mass, for enabling new quantum technologies and improving existing ones.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate the use of helium-3 atoms in tweezer arrays, focusing on their potential for continuous-variable quantum computing and tunable hopping for quantum simulation.
result: They show that helium-3's small mass provides advantages in these applications, potentially leading to faster operations and new capabilities.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, offering unique benefits for quantum computing and simulation.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom quantum computer in a cryogenic environment extends Rydberg lifetimes by reducing blackbody radiation, thereby mitigating a key error source in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg state lifetimes, which are degraded by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic apparatus to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate performance at cryogenic temperatures.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and reduced relaxation errors, leading to improved two-qubit gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable and effective strategy to enhance the performance of neutral-atom quantum computers by mitigating Rydberg decay errors.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas, a dissipative many-body platform, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
motivation: The study aims to explore non-Hermitian topology in a tunable dissipative quantum many-body system, which is of fundamental interest in quantum physics and may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a platform to engineer non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and measure spectral topology through experimental observations.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, demonstrating non-Hermitian topological effects.
conclusion: The work establishes cold Rydberg gases as a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics by decomposing the dynamics into standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient simulation method using photonic hardware.
method: They decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling execution on photonic simulators.
result: The approach allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical platform for simulating quantum field dynamics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding the limits of quantum advantage in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices requires characterizing the emergence of randomness and complexity in noisy circuits, particularly the phenomenon of anticoncentration.
method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of output distributions of random quantum circuits subject to local noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits universal behavior across different circuit architectures, with distinct regimes depending on circuit depth and noise strength, and that noise suppresses anticoncentration in a universal way.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for understanding the impact of noise on quantum randomness, with implications for quantum advantage experiments and benchmarking.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, potentially relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors propose a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze its many-body physics, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to study the emergence of blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. A comprehensive overview is needed to relate different approaches.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems, presenting a unified framework that highlights commonalities and differences.
result: It offers a structured overview of methods, including their applicability in quantum optics, quantum information, thermodynamics, and many-body physics.
conclusion: The unified framework aids in selecting appropriate simulation methods and fosters cross-disciplinary understanding of non-Markovian dynamics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: This review covers nonequilibrium dynamics in photoexcited Mott insulators, focusing on metastable states and control via strong fields.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems can reveal novel optical responses and quantum metastable phases.
method: The paper is a comprehensive review summarizing recent theoretical and experimental advances, discussing mechanisms and pathways for driving Mott insulators.
result: It highlights key mechanisms for photodoped carrier evolution and emergence of metastable orders like superconducting and magnetic states.
conclusion: Photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators offer a rich platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

tldr: This paper demonstrates that far-detuned attractive optical traps are not feasible for alkali Rydberg atoms due to ponderomotive antitrapping, and proposes alternative trapping strategies.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum simulation suffers from spin-motion coupling in Rydberg platforms, exacerbated by free expansion to avoid ponderomotive antitrapping. The authors investigate whether far-detuned attractive traps can mitigate this issue.
method: The authors analyze the ponderomotive potential for alkali Rydberg atoms in optical traps, considering both red- and blue-detuned traps, and calculate the resulting trap depths and lifetimes. They also explore alternative approaches such as using circular Rydberg states or dressing with off-resonant light.
result: They find that far-detuned attractive traps are not viable for alkali Rydberg atoms because the ponderomotive force is always repulsive for red-detuned light, and blue-detuned traps are inherently repulsive. They propose using circular Rydberg states or optical lattices with blue-detuned light to achieve trapping.
conclusion: The paper concludes that far-detuned attractive traps are impossible for alkali Rydberg atoms, and suggests alternative methods for trapping them without inducing spin-motion coupling.

conclusion: The findings suggest that driven nonequilibrium systems can exhibit Fermi-surface-like phenomena, offering new insights into non-Fermi liquid physics and potential experimental signatures.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their relation to quantum computation.
motivation: To provide a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems by treating space and time symmetrically, avoiding complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories.
method: The review synthesizes recent advances in discretizing time evolution on lattices, emphasizing the role of brickwork quantum circuits and space-time duality.
result: It presents a pedagogical framework connecting space-time duality to quantum computation, offering insights into exactly solvable many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The review highlights the far-reaching analogy with quantum computation as a central tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics.

In recent years, it has become possible to realize Coulomb crystals using laser-cooled trapped ions, and these systems allow for unprecedented control of experimental parameters. authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.

method: The review discusses the principles of tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, where a scanning tip acts as an optical antenna to confine light and achieve superresolution.
result: The technique enables atomic-scale spatial resolution in fluorescence imaging, revealing electronic and vibronic properties of molecules.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale imaging, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices, so understanding its mechanisms is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and simulation studies to propose a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation, involving surface defects, field emission, heating, and plasma formation.
result: They identify key interacting factors that trigger breakdown and suggest how these insights can guide improvements in high-power technologies.
conclusion: A unified understanding of vacuum breakdown can lead to more reliable and efficient accelerators and other high-field devices.

abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including magnetism, topology, and dynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize the rapidly evolving field of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials, which has challenged theories and opened new applications.
method: It is a review article that synthesizes current knowledge on magnetic phenomena, including experimental and theoretical advances.
result: The review highlights new phenomena such as topological magnetism, nonequilibrium dynamics, and interactions with light and electric fields.
conclusion: The field is expanding theoretical understanding and materials capabilities, with promising directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, discussing electronic structure, correlation effects, and observed phenomena.
result: The review highlights the rich physics of kagome metals, including topological flat bands, Dirac fermions, and various ordered states, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kagome metals serve as a platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological physics, but the paper is a review and not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.

tldr: This review summarizes how neutron star observations constrain the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.

abstract:

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.

tldr: This Colloquium reviews the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, focusing on multimessenger astronomy.
